noise_assumptions.notes: Conservative superconducting estimates. Not used by the Task B benchmark.

design_rationale: Our PS-Q1 circuit uses 4 qubits and a bidirectional CX ring (0-1, 1-2, 2-3, 3-0 in both directions) in every ansatz layer, so a 4-qubit ring with two-way links runs it with zero SWAPs; transpiled depth is 22 with 16 CX for 2 layers, versus 36 depth and 34 CX on the 5-qubit linear example. The single chord 0-2 closes a triangle (0-1-2) that QFT-3 needs for its three controlled-phase pairs, which removes the one SWAP a plain ring costs and gives 9 two-qubit gates. Every link is listed in both directions because the benchmark enforces direction and one-way links add single-qubit gates. The native set rx, ry, rz, h, cx covers our RY/RZ rotations directly and lets QFT-3 use native Hadamards, which lowered depth from 18 to 16 and raised noisy fidelity from 0.668 to 0.677. We stopped at one chord because extra links (a second chord, or a full triangle on 3 qubits) did not improve the benchmark further and add crosstalk risk in real devices.
